what_its_for: Miglitol is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It works by slowing down how quickly your body breaks down carbohydrates (sugars and starches) from food, which helps prevent your blood sugar from rising too high after meals.
how_to_take: Take miglitol by mouth with the very first bite of each main meal, three times a day. Swallow the tablet whole with a small amount of food. Do not skip meals when taking this medicine. If you miss a meal, skip that dose and wait until your next meal.
dosing: Your doctor will usually start you on a low dose (25 mg three times a day) and slowly increase it over several weeks based on how well your blood sugar is controlled and how well you tolerate the medicine. The usual maintenance dose is 50 mg three times a day, but your doctor may increase it up to 100 mg three times a day if needed. Always follow your doctor's instructions for your specific dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose at the start of a meal and you have already finished eating, skip that missed dose completely. Do NOT take it after the meal or double up on your next dose. Just take your next regular dose at the start of your next meal as usual.
storage: Store miglitol at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it in a dry place away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Keep it out of the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating large amounts of sugary or starchy foods, as this can make it harder to control your blood sugar. Be careful with alcohol, as it can affect your blood sugar levels. Avoid taking digestive enzyme supplements (like amylase or pancreatin) at the same time as miglitol, since they can make the medicine less effective. If you experience low blood sugar while also taking insulin or other diabetes medicines, use glucose tablets or glucose gel to treat it — NOT regular table sugar or fruit juice, because miglitol slows sugar absorption. Always carry glucose tablets with you.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe stomach pain, ongoing diarrhea or vomiting, yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems), signs of very low blood sugar such as shakiness, sweating, confusion, or fainting, or signs of very high blood sugar such as increased thirst, frequent urination, or blurred vision. Also call your doctor if you develop a skin rash or any unusual swelling.
when_it_works: Miglitol starts working at your very first dose by slowing sugar absorption during meals. However, it may take several weeks of regular use along with a healthy diet and exercise to see the full benefit on your blood sugar levels. Your doctor will check your blood sugar (HbA1c) periodically to monitor how well the medicine is working for you.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Miglitol is not recommended if you have moderate to severe kidney disease (creatinine above 2 mg/dL), as the medicine can build up in your body. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Miglitol is generally not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Children: Miglitol has not been approved for use in children. Elderly patients: Older adults may use this medicine, but should be monitored closely by their doctor.
